analysis.title: A Democratic Sweep: Oversight, Investigations, and Narrow Scope for Compromise
key_insights: Democrats have won both the House and Senate. Early polling had pointed to a more divided outcome with Democrats taking at least one chamber. The sweep gives the party more policy leverage heading into 2027.
The main dynamic of a Democratic Congress will be more oversight hearings and investigations. Democratic priority bills are likely to face frequent presidential vetoes.
BNY expects more political scrutiny of certain sectors and companies, slower confirmation votes, and fewer significant legislative changes.
Budget standoffs and potential government shutdowns are likely, though limited bipartisan spending deals are possible.
Solar and wind could regain policy support, slowing the fossil-fuel momentum of the prior two years.
Healthcare segments (hospitals, life sciences tools, the ACA and Medicaid) could benefit as Democrats push to restore NIH and ACA-related funding.
Healthcare may offer the most room for compromise with the administration, especially on pharmaceutical pricing controls, which would be a challenge for the sector.

A Democratic Congress is likely to agree to modest defense spending increases in exchange for funding Democratic priorities. Any supplemental funds tied to the Iran conflict could face tougher scrutiny.
Crypto and unconstrained AI and data center expansion could face added policy headwinds. Democrats plan to expand AI oversight through a new House Select Committee.

States may lead on AI regulation because there are no federal guidelines or legislation and too few votes for federal pre-emption. Texas, Georgia, Ohio and Pennsylvania are the key states for the AI buildout, through governors' races, utility commissions and state legislatures that shape regulatory approvals, grid costs and tax incentives.

Trump administration tariffs look likely to continue, with Section 301 reinforcing tariff levels and continued tax-incentive support for U.S. manufacturing reshoring. Democrats appear supportive of protecting key manufacturing sectors while reducing tariffs on certain consumer goods for affordability.
BNY sees little chance of fiscal consolidation after the midterms. At least one government shutdown, potentially paired with another debt-ceiling standoff, is likely in 2027.
The midterm results signal policy direction, with more consequential changes and an unusually broad range of outcomes in play for the 2028 presidential election.
